description_extension.message: Explains, without judging, the persuasion devices a web page uses, and grades its trustworthiness. Free (AGPL-3.0), self-hostable.

erreur_analyse_perdue.message: The browser stopped the analysis before it finished. Chrome shuts the extension down as soon as it considers it idle, and work under way disappears with it. Start the analysis again.

erreur_page_inaccessible.message: Lynceus cannot reach this page. If it is an internal browser page or the Web Store, it cannot be analysed. Otherwise: start again with a right-click → “Analyse this page with Lynceus” (access expires when you navigate away). You can also turn on the passive badge in the settings so that this button keeps working after navigation.

erreur_delai_depasse.message: The instance did not answer within the allotted time ($1 s). The configured model provider may be slow or unavailable; you can raise this delay in the settings, or try again later.

erreur_instance_injoignable.message: Lynceus instance unreachable ($1). Is the server running? The address can be changed in the extension options.

erreur_cle_requise.message: Enter your access key in the extension settings.

erreur_portail_injoignable.message: Portal unreachable ($1). Check the address and your connection.

erreur_contenu_introuvable.message: No main content found on this page (home page, web app… ?).

erreur_billet_invalide.message: That portal did not return a usable key.

motif_extrait_hors_contexte.message: A quotation is taken out of context

motif_categorie_erronee.message: The category is wrong (e.g. satire misread)

motif_note_injustifiee.message: The grade does not match the content

motif_droit_de_reponse.message: I publish this site and I dispute this

panneau_profil_avertissement.message: This describes other pages on this site, not this one: its content has not been read yet.

panneau_repos_texte.message: Lynceus reads the content, then describes the persuasion techniques it uses: excerpts, explanations and strong points. You draw the conclusion.

panneau_repos_vie_privee.message: Nothing is sent without this action: the content of the page goes to your Lynceus instance only when you ask for the analysis.

panneau_reconnaissance_texte.message: Lynceus can also recognise already-analysed pages on its own, and show their grade without you clicking.

panneau_attente_extraction.message: Extracting the content, locally in your browser…

panneau_attente_analyse.message: Analysis under way, the model is reading the page…

panneau_contestations_enregistrees.message: $1 dispute(s) already recorded on this analysis.

panneau_deja_annuaire_cache.message: Already in the directory, instant answer

panneau_detections_ecartees.message: $1 detection(s) proposed by the model were discarded by the server (quotation not found in the page, or outside the catalogue).

panneau_contestation_impossible.message: This analysis cannot be disputed from this panel (no identifier).

panneau_formulaire_invite.message: Explain in a few words (10 characters minimum)…

panneau_formulaire_trop_court.message: Please say a little more: 10 characters minimum.

options_instance_aide.message: The address of the server that analyses pages and keeps the directory. You can use your own: the server kit is free software and self-hostable.

options_badge_intitule.message: Show the grade on the icon, and a discreet outline on pages graded at risk (D/E), when a page you visit is already in the directory, without having to click “Analyse”.

options_badge_aide.message:
What Lynceus sends over the network does not change: only a hash (fingerprint) of the page address, never the address itself nor its content, and nothing is logged. The content of a page is sent only when you click “Analyse this page”, and that text is then passed by the instance to the model provider it uses, sometimes outside the European Union.

What this setting changes: Chrome will ask you to allow Lynceus to access all your pages (a technical browser permission). That is what makes it possible to know the address continuously (for the badge) and to draw or remove the outline, including on sites that navigate internally such as YouTube. This permission also makes the panel's “Analyse this page” button reliable after navigation (the one-off access granted by the right-click expires each time you move).

Off by default. Without this setting, everything stays at the minimum: an explicit action (right-click) is needed on every page.

options_cle_aide.message: Some instances require a key to run analyses (directory lookups stay open). A Lynceus key is not an account: it contains no name, no address, no identifier about you, only an expiry date and a number of analyses per day. Leave it empty if your instance does not ask for one.

options_portail_aide.message: Don't have one? A portal can issue one immediately, and will fill in the address of the instance it gives access to at the same time. The portal is a separate service from the instance: it alone signs keys.

options_obtenir_cle.message: Get a key from this portal

options_delai_aide.message: Maximum time an analysis may take before it is abandoned. A timer and a “Cancel” button remain available in the panel while you wait. This delay is only a last resort if the connection hangs without ever answering. The server has its own ceiling (180 s by default, up to 360 s with an automatic retry): keep this value well above it so that a legitimate analysis is never cut short.

options_permission_refusee.message: Permission refused. The passive badge and outline stay off.

options_prompt.message: Analysis prompt: v$1 · $2 techniques in the catalogue

options_cle_requise.message: This instance requires an access key for analyses.

options_transparence.message: It publishes its methodology: that is the Lynceus transparency contract.

options_instance_injoignable.message: Instance unreachable ($1). Is the server running?

accueil_chapo.message: The lookout for information. Lynceus describes the persuasion techniques a page uses, without judging: you draw the conclusion.

accueil_inscription_titre.message: First, connect Lynceus to an instance

accueil_inscription_aide.message: Lynceus does not work on its own: it needs an instance to analyse pages. A portal can point you to one and issue you an access key: no account, no email address, one click.

accueil_cle_existante.message: A key is already stored. Asking for a new one will replace it.

accueil_cle_contenu.message: the key contains no name, no address, no account identifier: only an expiry date and a number of analyses per day;

accueil_cle_auto_heberge.message: if you host your own instance, you need no key at all: just enter its address in the settings.

accueil_reconnaissance_titre.message: Would you rather be told automatically?

accueil_reconnaissance_aide.message: Lynceus can recognise pages already analysed by others, with nothing for you to do:

accueil_reconnaissance_1.message: the grade appears on the icon as soon as a known page opens;

accueil_reconnaissance_2.message: the panel shows the card straight away, without clicking “Analyse”;

accueil_reconnaissance_3.message: a discreet outline surrounds pages graded at risk (D or E);

accueil_reconnaissance_4.message: works on sites that change content without reloading (YouTube and the like).

accueil_reconnaissance_activee.message: Automatic recognition is on. You can close this tab and browse normally.

accueil_permission_refusee.message: Permission refused. Lynceus still works through the right-click menu. You can turn this on later in the settings.

accueil_plus_tard.message: Understood. Use the right-click menu, then “Analyse this page”. Automatic recognition stays available in the settings.

accueil_ce_qui_est_envoye.message: What Lynceus sends, in both cases. To recognise a page, only a fingerprint (hash) of its address is sent: neither the address itself, nor its content, and nothing is logged. The content of a page is transmitted only when you click “Analyse this page”. That text then goes to the instance, which passes it to the language model provider it uses, sometimes established outside the European Union. That is unavoidable in order to analyse, and a public instance must set it out in its privacy policy. A self-hosted instance with a local model sends nothing outside. Chrome will ask for access to your pages: that is the technical permission needed to read the address continuously and draw the outline, and it changes nothing about what travels over the network. Reversible at any time in the settings.

accueil_sans_activer_titre.message: Without turning it on, Lynceus still works

accueil_sans_activer_aide.message: Right-click on a page, then “🔭 Analyse this page with Lynceus”. Permissions kept to the strict minimum, but every page needs that action, including after navigating.
